conviction_note: Peer and capex evidence after Cisco last spoke (Arista's 2027 guide of ~$18.5bn against $16.4bn expected, Celestica networking +68%, hyperscalers all guiding 2027 capex up) points to a strong AI-order and FY27 guide; against it, Q4-CY26 DRAM contracts up another 10-20% QoQ land squarely on the Q2 gross-margin guide, which is the line this stock sold on in February (-12.3%) and August (-8.4%, despite a guide far above consensus). The findings sum to about +0.9 and the scaled number is near flat (p_up 51 x abs 9.0 = +0.18): the reaction function, beats-and-raises sold twice on margin, keeps p_up near 50 even though the fundamental read (print_vs_bar) is a modest beat.
bar: Q1 FY27 company guide revenue $18.0-18.2bn, non-GAAP GM 65-66%, non-GAAP EPS $1.32-1.34 (https://investor.cisco.com/news/news-details/2026/CISCO-REPORTS-FOURTH-QUARTER-AND-FISCAL-YEAR-2026-EARNINGS/default.aspx, 2026-08-12); consensus $18.09-18.12bn / $1.32-1.33 per Zacks and Investing.com (https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/cisco-earnings-preview-eps-margins-and-guidance-in-focus-93CH-5019656, 2026-11-11), i.e. on the guide midpoint. Q2 (Jan-quarter) revenue consensus $17.83bn and FY27 $72.94bn / $5.10 (same Investing.com source) against FY27 guide $72.2-73.4bn / $5.05-5.11. Sell-side bull bar: JPMorgan expects FY27 growth guide raised to 16-17% from ~15% and AI revenue target to $8.5bn from $7.5bn (https://www.tipranks.com/news/cisco-q1-earnings-preview-heres-what-analysts-and-options-traders-expect-from-csco-stock, 2026-11-12). No sourced Q2 gross-margin consensus found.
positioning_check: Short interest 51.1M shares, about 1.3-1.5% of float, 2.3 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 FINRA settlement (down from 57.7M / 4.4 days at 09-15) per https://equibles.com/stocks/csco/shortinterest and https://tapeboard.com/stock/CSCO/short-squeeze/ (tapeboard shows 3.2 DTC); October settlements not found. Not a crowded short. Baseline: 25d skew -0.87 vol points (balanced, calls fractionally bid), put/call OI 0.57, straddle-implied move 8.75% (ATM IV 147.9%, spread 13.6% of mid). Tape: +6.29% over 5 days, -7.38% over 20 days, -21.7% from the 52-week high; the 20-day drop includes a ~8% fall on 2026-11-05 when Morgan Stanley downgraded to Equal-weight on the same day the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq 5.5% in a post-election AI-infrastructure selloff.

findings.finding: Arista (the closest pure-play peer, reported 2026-11-03, after Cisco last spoke on 2026-08-12) printed Q3 revenue $3.66bn, +58.5% YoY, against $3.31bn consensus, guided Q4 to $3.9-4.0bn and guided 2027 revenue to about $18.5bn against $16.4bn expected, with AI networking sales seen roughly doubling to ~$7bn in 2027; the stock rose 5.0% the next day. This points to hyperscaler AI networking demand running above what was expected in August, supporting Cisco's AI orders (benchmark: $4.0bn in Q4 FY26) and a raise to the FY27 guide ($72.2-73.4bn; JPM expects a raise to 16-17% growth).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Orders/guide surprises have cut both ways: May 2026 (big AI order and guide raise) +13.41%; August 2026 (Q1 guide $18.1bn vs $16.8bn consensus, FY27 far above) -8.40% because gross margin fell to 66.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: Cisco fell ~8% two days after this print, in the 2026-11-05 market selloff, and sits 21.7% below its high at ~20x forward EPS; if the peer read-through were priced Cisco would have tracked Arista's +5% on 11-04 and held it. Consensus for Cisco's FY27 ($72.94bn) is still inside the company's August range, so no raise is in the published numbers.
findings.independence: Celestica's Q3 (finding 2) and hyperscaler 2027 capex commentary (finding 3) point the same way from different counterparties: https://finviz.com/news/408117/celestica-announces-third-quarter-2026-financial-results-and-will-hold-2026-investor-and-analyst-day ; Arista's 2027 guide and the next-day move are also in https://www.tikr.com/blog/arista-sinks-11-ciena-down-15-as-ai-selloff-deepens-after-democratic-sweep and https://www.trefis.com/stock/anet/articles/623355/why-is-arista-stock-falling/2026-11-06

findings.finding: Celestica Q3 2026 (quarter to 30 Sep, overlapping most of Cisco's Aug-Oct Q1): revenue $5.83bn +83%, Connectivity & Cloud Solutions $4.87bn +102%, networking +68% on 800G and early 1.6T hyperscaler switch ramps, 2026 revenue outlook raised to $21bn from $20.5bn and Q4 networking seen +~65%. Confirms hyperscaler switch spending in Cisco's quarter, though Celestica builds white-box switches that partly compete with Cisco's Silicon One/8000 systems.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same AI-order line as finding 1: +13.41% (May 2026), -8.40% (Aug 2026, margin-driven).
findings.why_not_priced: A supplier/competitor print rarely moves Cisco's estimates; Cisco's Q1 and FY27 revenue consensus sit on the August guide rather than above it, which is what you would not see if hyperscaler networking strength after August were in the numbers.
findings.independence: Arista (finding 1) is a separate company and source; both are proxies for hyperscaler networking demand, not Cisco's own numbers. White-box share gain is a partial offset for Cisco.

findings.finding: October hyperscaler prints held or lifted 2026 capex (Amazon ~$220bn held, Alphabet $195-205bn held, Meta floor raised to $135-145bn) and every one said 2027 capex rises significantly; Moody's marked hyperscaler capex up $85bn toward ~$1trn in 2027. Cisco's $9.3bn FY26 hyperscaler AI orders depend on this spend; management said FY27 AI orders should be 'meaningfully higher' than $9.3bn.
findings.source_date: 2026-10/11 (post-October hyperscaler earnings; date from search listing, not verified in URL path)
findings.why_not_priced: Broadly known macro; included because Cisco has not spoken since and its FY27 AI revenue target ($7.5bn) predates these 2027 statements. Macro-to-company transmission, so small.
findings.independence: Proxy. Same direction as findings 1 and 2 but independent sources (hyperscaler releases); capex figures summarised via search, see also https://walnutinvest.com/stats/ai-capex-statistics

findings.finding: Memory cost pressure on the next guide: TrendForce sees conventional DRAM contract prices up 10-15% QoQ in 4Q26 (later headline ~20%) and server DIMMs up double digits, on top of 13-18% in 3Q26. The 3Q26 increase was public in July and so sits inside Cisco's Aug-12 Q1 GM guide (65-66% vs 66.3% Q4 and 68.1% a year ago), but the 4Q26 step lands in Cisco's Q2 (Nov-Jan) and will shape the Q2 gross-margin guide, together with heavier lower-margin hyperscaler hardware mix; the 10-K says part of Cisco's memory LTAs are fixed-quantity at variable market prices. Offsets: list price increases (effective Nov 7, finding 5) and 30+ memory redesign programs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin is the line this stock trades on: Feb 2026 GM 67.5% vs 68.14% expected, -12.32%; Aug 2026 GM 66.3% (from 68.4%) with a guide far above consensus, -8.40%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced (MS downgrade cites AI gross-margin headwinds; Zacks flags memory). Not fully: no sourced Q2 GM consensus exists, and the company's 'slight headwind through FY27' framing from August predates the 4Q26 contract step; if it were priced the stock would not have rebounded 6.3% in five days into the print with balanced skew.
findings.independence: TrendForce Sep-30 forecast (10-15%, https://evertiq.com/news/2026-10-02-ai-keeps-memory-prices-climbing-in-q4-as-consumer-demand-weakens); 10-K variable-priced memory LTA language (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000858877/000085887726000132/csco-20260725.htm); MS downgrade note (https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/cisco-earnings-preview-eps-margins-and-guidance-in-focus-93CH-5019656). The 10-K is shared with finding 6.

findings.finding: Cisco told partners on 2026-10-24/26 of list price increases effective 2026-11-07, mainly networking and security software at mid-single-digit average plus unnamed hardware (Splunk excluded). Cisco's Q1 FY27 ended around 2026-10-24, so any ordering ahead of the increase falls in Q2 orders/revenue and supports the Q2 revenue guide, and the realised price helps the Q2 GM guide against memory (finding 4). Morgan Stanley warns such ordering-ahead flatters near-term sales, so the market may discount it as low quality.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prior price actions (Feb 2026 call: 'already raised prices') did not prevent the -12.32% GM reaction that quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: Trade-press only (CRN/ChannelInsider/SDxCentral); the wire previews do not tie the Nov-7 timing to the Q2 guide. If priced, Q2 revenue consensus ($17.83bn) would sit above the seasonal run-rate implied by the FY27 range rather than below the $18.2bn quarterly average it implies.
findings.independence: https://www.sdxcentral.com/news/cisco-hikes-software-prices-in-portfolio-rebalance/ ; MS pull-forward warning via https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/cisco-earnings-preview-eps-margins-and-guidance-in-focus-93CH-5019656 (cuts the other way on quality).

findings.finding: FY26 10-K (filed 2026-09-02): inventory up 80% and inventory purchase commitments up 126% YoY (about $17.2bn vs $7.6bn per sec-api), tied mainly to Silicon One and other products for hyperscaler demand, including multi-year fixed-dollar supply commitments and fixed-quantity memory agreements at variable prices. Asked what the commitment buys: it corroborates a shipping ramp behind the $7.5bn FY27 AI revenue target (positive for revenue conversion), while the variable-price memory piece is the margin exposure already counted in finding 4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior reaction on inventory/commitments disclosed; revenue beats have been bought (May +13.41%) or overridden by margin (Aug -8.40%).
findings.why_not_priced: Public since September; filed because the size of the build implies conversion capacity above the guide, and previews anchor on orders, not on supply in hand. Largely priced; small.
findings.independence: https://sec-api.io/insights/cisco-csco-fy2026-annual-results-analysis-ai-infrastructure-orders-purchase-commitments-margins-peers-and-scenarios-to-fy2030 (secondary reading of the same 10-K, so not independent). The memory-pricing half is merged into finding 4 to avoid double counting.

findings.finding: Expectations reset since August: the stock went into the August print up >60% YTD near its highs and fell 8.4% on a guide raise; it now sits 21.7% below its 52-week high at ~19-20x forward EPS after Morgan Stanley's 2026-11-05 downgrade to Equal-weight ($120 from $135, citing high expectations and AI gross-margin headwinds) coincided with an S&P -4.4% / Nasdaq -5.5% session. Short interest is low (1.3-1.5% of float) and skew balanced, so neither a squeeze nor a crowded long; the bar for a margin disappointment is lower than in August.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Into high expectations it sold beats (Feb -12.32%, Aug -8.40%); into a lower bar in May it rose +13.41%.
findings.why_not_priced: The de-rating was largely a market-wide move (XLK -8% that day) rather than Cisco-specific news, so it may have taken out more than the downgrade's content; but the +6.3% 5-day rebound has already recovered part of it.
findings.independence: S&P/Nasdaq/XLK moves from https://www.trefis.com/stock/anet/articles/623355/why-is-arista-stock-falling/2026-11-06 ; downgrade details from https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/cisco-earnings-preview-eps-margins-and-guidance-in-focus-93CH-5019656 ; short interest from https://equibles.com/stocks/csco/shortinterest

findings.finding: The Q1 bar is the guide: consensus $18.09-18.12bn / $1.32-1.33 sits on the $18.0-18.2bn / $1.32-1.34 midpoint, and management said in August that ex-hyperscaler double-digit order momentum carried into Q1; Cisco beat Q4 revenue consensus by ~2.6% ($17.25bn vs $16.82bn). A modest revenue/EPS beat is likely but lands inside what the company guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Reported-quarter beats have not decided the reaction: Aug 2026 beat on EPS ($1.22 vs $1.17) and revenue, -8.40%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: a beat inside the guide is what the company told the market to expect.
findings.independence: Q1 momentum statement via https://indrastocks.substack.com/p/csco-q1-fy2027-earnings-prep (secondary summary of the August call).

baseline_tension: Balanced skew and a +6.3% five-day rebound give no directional statement to fight; peer evidence leans up and the memory step leans down on the exact line (gross margin) that drove the last two large negative reactions, so the evidence offsets and p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold beat-and-raise twice on margin): Arista peer finding 1.0 -> 0.7, Celestica 0.4 -> 0.3, capex 0.5 -> 0.3; p_up 52 -> 51.
Lesson 6 (finding inside what the company guided): Q1 reported-quarter beat 0.3 -> 0.1.
Lesson 7 (positioning): short interest looked up before the negative memory finding; not crowded, so the -1.5 stands.
Lesson 4 (financing/commitments are a question): 10-K purchase commitments read as funding a ramp, kept +0.2, margin half merged into the memory finding.
Left standing: memory/GM finding -1.5, price-increase +0.3, positioning +0.5, abs_move 9.0.
